failureMode: Primary tank rupture initiating event frequency, value quoted from the CRBR analysis
table: Section 5.2.8 Rapid Loss of Circulation, text on pages 5-58 and 5-59
method: Quoted from the CRBR analysis, based on leak before rupture arguments and fracture mechanics.

component: Primary tank (vessel), FFTF
failureMode: Primary tank rupture initiating event frequency, value quoted from the FFTF analysis
table: Section 5.2.8 Rapid Loss of Circulation, text on pages 5-58 and 5-59
method: Quoted from the FFTF analysis and adopted for EBR-II.

component: Guard vessel, FFTF
failureMode: Guard vessel leak in the presence of sodium, value quoted from the FFTF analysis
table: Section 5.2.8 Rapid Loss of Circulation, text on pages 5-58 and 5-59
method: Quoted from the FFTF analysis.

component: Vessels in higher pressure and more corrosive environments
failureMode: Ratio of rupture to leak frequency, lowest value in the range
table: Section 5.2.8 Rapid Loss of Circulation, text on pages 5-58 and 5-59
method: Typical ratio for higher pressure and more corrosive environments, printed as 1E-2 to 1E-4.

component: Vessels in higher pressure and more corrosive environments
failureMode: Ratio of rupture to leak frequency, highest value in the range
table: Section 5.2.8 Rapid Loss of Circulation, text on pages 5-58 and 5-59
method: Typical ratio for higher pressure and more corrosive environments, printed as 1E-2 to 1E-4. The conservative 1E-2 is used for the EBR-II guard vessel.

component: EBR-II guard vessel
failureMode: Rupture frequency from the leak frequency and the 1E-2 ratio
table: Section 5.2.8 Rapid Loss of Circulation, text on pages 5-58 and 5-59
method: FFTF guard vessel leak frequency 1.0E-4 times the rupture to leak ratio 1E-2.

component: EBR-II guard vessel
failureMode: Rupture frequency increased for lack of inspection
table: Section 5.2.8 Rapid Loss of Circulation, text on pages 5-58 and 5-59
method: Increased by an order of magnitude because the guard vessel cannot be inspected and the annulus gas system is not tested.

component: Initiating event LCRA, rapid loss of circulation
failureMode: Frequency for rupture of both primary and guard vessels
table: Section 5.2.8 Rapid Loss of Circulation, text on pages 5-58 and 5-59
method: Requires rupture of both vessels and is below the screening frequency, so LCRA sequences are not quantified. Table 5.9 lists 1.1E-13 under other methods and 1.0E-13 as final.

component: Breached Fuel Test Facility (BFTF)
failureMode: Breach of dry-well and terminal box allowing primary sodium removal (LCDL contributor)
table: Section 5.2.9 Delayed Loss of Circulation (LCDL), text on pages 5-60 and 5-61
method: Frequency from reference 5.16, with flow under the BFTF of only 10 to 20 gpm.

component: Primary sodium purification and sampling system
failureMode: Piping leak with syphon break failure (LCDL contributor)
table: Section 5.2.9 Delayed Loss of Circulation (LCDL), text on pages 5-60 and 5-61
method: Calculated initiator frequency for syphoning primary sodium through a purification system leak.

component: IHX tubes with secondary sodium system
failureMode: IHX tube failure combined with dump, vent and storage tank failures (LCDL contributor)
table: Section 5.2.9 Delayed Loss of Circulation (LCDL), text on pages 5-60 and 5-61
method: Calculated frequency for IHX tube failure with a dump, dump valves stuck open, a plugged argon vent and a storage tank rupture.

component: Initiating event TAIR, transient with loss of instrument air
failureMode: Annual frequency from plant data, text value
table: Section 5.2.10 Support System Failures, text on page 5-62
method: Printed in the text as based upon plant data. Tables 5.9 and 5.10 give 2.5E-1 per year.

component: Initiating event MELF, local fault, metal experiment pin failure
failureMode: Yearly average of metal experiment element breaches
table: Section 5.2.12 Local Faults, text on pages 5-63 and 5-64
method: About 90 metal experiment element breaches since about 1970 give a yearly average of 4.5 with error factor 3, and the exposure in years is not printed. Lognormal from the printed mean and error factor, with median = mean/exp(s^2/2) and s = ln(EF)/1.645.

component: Initiating event SFPB, local fault, partial subassembly blockage
failureMode: Partial subassembly blockages from orificing errors
table: Section 5.2.12 Local Faults, text on pages 5-63 and 5-64
method: Three occasions of partial blockage give an initiating frequency of 1.4E-1 per year. The exposure is not printed with this count.

component: Initiating event SFLE, local fault, subassembly loading error
failureMode: Subassembly loading errors in 25 years of operation
table: Section 5.2.12 Local Faults, text on pages 5-63 and 5-64
method: One loading error in 25 years of operation, detected before reactor operation, gives 6.0E-2 per year.

component: Anticipatory or normal shutdowns
failureMode: Annual frequency, part of the 11.11 per year scram and shutdown total
table: Section 5.2.13 Final Initiating Event Frequencies, text on page 5-64
method: Sum of the anticipatory and normal shutdown mean frequencies printed in the text.

component: Scrams other than anticipatory or normal shutdowns
failureMode: Annual frequency of the remaining scrams
table: Section 5.2.13 Final Initiating Event Frequencies, text on page 5-64
method: Remainder of the 11.11 per year total, dominated by balance of plant faults, primary pump faults, spurious scrams (0.7) and electrical supply faults.

component: Electrical supply faults (LONP and LOCP)
failureMode: Annual frequency of scrams from electrical supply faults
table: Section 5.2.13 Final Initiating Event Frequencies, text on page 5-64
method: Printed in the text as 0.2 per year, the sum of the LONP and LOCP mean frequencies.

component: Flow sensor trip point verification, events RHU1A1QL, RHU1B1QL, RHU1C1QL and RHU1D1QL

component: Flow sensor trip point verification, events RHU1A1QL, RHU1B1QL, RHU1C1QL and RHU1D1QL
failureMode: Value used in the loss of flow fault tree, modeled as channel failure

method: The report states that the loss of flow fault tree models these errors as events that lead to channel failure at a reduced probability of 1E-6.

component: Subassembly outlet temperature channel calibration (event printed as RHU3AQL, tree events RHU3A1QL to RHU3D1QL)

component: Subassembly outlet temperature trip point setting (event RHU302QL)

component: High flux trip point setting at 110 percent of authorized power (event RHU201QL)

table: Section 8.2.2.4 Wide Range Nuclear Channel Trip Points, text on pages 8-31 and 8-35

component: Master selector switch (MSSW) (event CSWMSCCL)

table: Section 8.4.4 Acts of Commission, text on pages 8-64 and 8-65

table: Section 8.5.1 Recovery of Electrical Systems, text on pages 8-66 and 8-67
method: Screening value. The loss of normal power to a bus is annunciated and its cause is usually obvious, so diagnosis dominates the error.

component: Recovery of decay heat removal after loss of both shutdown coolers with the secondary loop drained (event B0001Z00)
failureMode: Failure to recover from loss of decay heat removal
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Total of human event tree ARGI (Tables 8.29 and 8.30), estimated conservatively from NUREG/CR-1278 Table 20-1 with only 60 minutes assumed for diagnosis and action. Refill of the secondary loop takes 48 hours from cold pipes or about 3.5 hours if the pipes are heated.

component: Recovery of the shutdown coolers (event DHU000OL)
failureMode: Human error, failure to recover coolers, dominated by failure to diagnose
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: The recoverable loss of shutdown coolers is modeled in the decay heat removal trees and is dominated by the failure to diagnose the problem, printed as 10^-6.

component: Recovery after a spurious trip in a cooling system such as shield cooling
failureMode: Noncorrective action after a flow alarm with a recovery procedure
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Generic values used for recovery of spurious breaker trips. A flow alarm signals a more urgent need for action than a current, voltage or power signal.

component: Recovery after a spurious trip in a cooling system such as shield cooling
failureMode: Noncorrective action after a current, voltage or power alarm with a recovery procedure
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Generic values used for recovery of spurious breaker trips. A flow alarm signals a more urgent need for action than a current, voltage or power signal.

component: Recovery after a spurious trip in a cooling system such as shield cooling
failureMode: Noncorrective action after a flow alarm in troubleshooting mode
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Generic values used for recovery of spurious breaker trips. A flow alarm signals a more urgent need for action than a current, voltage or power signal.

component: Recovery after a spurious trip in a cooling system such as shield cooling
failureMode: Noncorrective action after a current, voltage or power alarm in troubleshooting mode
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Generic values used for recovery of spurious breaker trips. A flow alarm signals a more urgent need for action than a current, voltage or power signal.

component: Shield cooling system circuit breaker (event HHU002YL)
failureMode: No recovery action to reset circuit breaker
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Value used for the basic events of the shield cooling and thimble cooling systems.

component: Thimble cooling system circuit breaker (event THU002YL)
failureMode: No recovery action to reset circuit breaker
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Value used for the basic events of the shield cooling and thimble cooling systems.

component: Shield cooling filter R8-FL-717 (event HHU01BSZ)
failureMode: No recovery action for clogged filter (shift to the other filter)
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: The filter shift is performed yearly for filter replacement.

component: Shield cooling motor damper (event HHU003SL)
failureMode: No recovery action to use damper manual handwheel
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Handwheel use is taught in operator qualification without repeat training, but training covers a similar steam isolation valve.

component: Shield cooling motor damper (event HHU003YL)
failureMode: No recovery action to use damper manual handwheel
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Handwheel use is taught in operator qualification without repeat training, but training covers a similar steam isolation valve.

component: Thimble cooling motor damper (event THU003SL)
failureMode: No recovery action to use damper manual handwheel
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Handwheel use is taught in operator qualification without repeat training, but training covers a similar steam isolation valve.

component: Stack exhaust system damper (event HHU004SL)
failureMode: No recovery action to move damper manually, dampers operated by non-EBR-II personnel
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: A higher value is used because non-EBR-II personnel operate these dampers.

component: Shield cooling or thimble cooling pneumatic damper (event code printed as HHU004SL)
failureMode: No recovery action to move damper manually by removing a connecting pin or bolt
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: The action is taught in qualification with annual training. The report lists the same event code as for the stack exhaust dampers.

component: Thimble cooling cross-connect damper (event THO01BSZ)
failureMode: No recovery action to cross-connect shield cooling
table: Section 8.5.2 Recovery of Decay Heat Removal Systems, text on pages 8-67 to 8-73
method: Opening a manual damper cross-connects thimble cooling to shield cooling when thimble cooling flow is lost.

component: Stuck reactor console master switch (event CSWMSWCZ)
failureMode: Operator fails to free stuck switch
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: The operator freed the switch in the one event when it stuck (plant data, reference 8.6).

component: Push button PSB2 (event CSWPSBCL)
failureMode: Operator fails to push PSB2, hourly rate
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: Based on the NUREG/CR-1278 page 13-9 value of 3E-3 per demand for a similar error, converted for a demand to set the switch to neutral every 18 hours.

component: Push button PSB2 (event CSWPSBCL)
failureMode: Value quoted from NUREG/CR-1278 page 13-9 for a similar error
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: Handbook basis of event CSWPSBCL before conversion to an hourly rate.

component: Reactor console master switch (MSW) (event CSWMS4CZ)
failureMode: Operator holds MSW up instead of down
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: NUREG/CR-1278 Table 12-1 value of 5E-4 with a performance shaping factor of 50 for stress between moderately high and extremely high (page 17-17). The report calls the result a mean. No error factor is printed.

component: Reactor console master switch (MSW) (event CSWMS4CZ)
failureMode: Value quoted from NUREG/CR-1278 Table 12-1
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: Handbook basis of event CSWMS4CZ before the performance shaping factor.

component: Reactor console master switch (MSW) (event CSWMS4CZ)
failureMode: Performance shaping factor for stress between moderately high and extremely high
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: Multiplies the NUREG/CR-1278 Table 12-1 HEP of 5E-4 (stress levels from page 17-17).

component: Reactor console master switch held by an unauthorized person (event CSWMSICL)
failureMode: Operators fail to free MSW from unauthorized person
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: NUREG/CR-1278 Table 20-16 sets failure to detect an error of commission at 10 times the basic HEP, which gives 0.1 from the 0.01 basis of CSWCONCZ. High flux alarms are judged to reduce this by at least a factor of 2. No credit is taken for two operators.

component: Reactor console master switch held by an unauthorized person (event CSWMSICL)
failureMode: Multiplier for failure to detect an error of commission (NUREG/CR-1278 Table 20-16)
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: Applied to the 0.01 basic HEP of event CSWCONCZ to give 0.1.

component: Reactor console master switch held by an unauthorized person (event CSWMSICL)
failureMode: Reduction divisor for high flux alarms, at least 2
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: The value of 0.1 is divided by this factor to give the 5E-2 used.

component: Control rod relay closure (event CSWMS3CZ)
failureMode: Operator closes relay, then fails to compensate with controlling rod
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: Printed as (0.1)(1) + (0.9)(3E-3)(5), where 0.1 is the probability that rod 4 is the controlling rod, 3E-3 is the HEP of item 7 on page 13-6 of NUREG/CR-1278 and 5 is the factor for moderately high stress.

component: Control rod relay closure (event CSWMS3CZ)
failureMode: Probability that rod 4 is the controlling rod
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: Conditional probability used in the HEP of event CSWMS3CZ.

component: Control rod relay closure (event CSWMS3CZ)
failureMode: Probability that rod 4 is not the controlling rod
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: Conditional probability used in the HEP of event CSWMS3CZ.

component: Control rod relay closure (event CSWMS3CZ)
failureMode: HEP quoted from NUREG/CR-1278 page 13-6 item 7 for balancing rod 4 with another rod
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: Handbook basis before the stress factor of 5.

component: Control rod relay closure (event CSWMS3CZ)
failureMode: Performance shaping factor for moderately high stress
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: Multiplies the HEP of 3E-3 because rod 4 moves before it is expected to.

component: Second control rod compensation (event CHU0P1CL)
failureMode: Operator decides to compensate with 2nd rod
table: Section 8.5.3 Recovery of Control Rod Malfunctions, text on pages 8-74 and 8-75
method: There is no procedure for this action.

component: Breached Fuel Test Facility (BFTF) sodium piping
failureMode: Sodium or NaK fire initiating event frequency (piping leak)
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Leak frequency from the generic piping failure rate of 3E-9 per hour per foot, the piping length, reactor runs of 2400 hours and about three runs per year (Section 10.2.3.2, page 10-15). The text states that a BFTF leak is not considered a significant fire initiator.

component: Fuel Element Rupture Detection (FERD) system sodium piping
failureMode: Sodium or NaK fire initiating event frequency (piping leak)
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Leak frequency from the generic piping failure rate of 3E-9 per hour per foot, the piping length, reactor runs of 2400 hours and about three runs per year (Section 10.2.3.2, page 10-15).

component: Primary sodium purification system piping out of cell
failureMode: Sodium or NaK fire initiating event frequency (piping leak)
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Leak frequency from the generic piping failure rate of 3E-9 per hour per foot, the piping length, reactor runs of 2400 hours and about three runs per year (Section 10.2.3.2, page 10-15). Note [1]: limited by the syphon break system. In-cell piping is excluded.

component: Secondary sodium piping within containment
failureMode: Sodium or NaK fire initiating event frequency (piping leak)
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Leak frequency from the generic piping failure rate of 3E-9 per hour per foot, the piping length, reactor runs of 2400 hours and about three runs per year (Section 10.2.3.2, page 10-15). This is the initiator SSFR of Figure 10.3.

component: Shutdown cooler NaK piping
failureMode: Sodium or NaK fire initiating event frequency (piping leak)
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Leak frequency from the generic piping failure rate of 3E-9 per hour per foot, the piping length, reactor runs of 2400 hours and about three runs per year (Section 10.2.3.2, page 10-15). This is the initiator SDFR of Figure 10.4, for a leak in either cooler system.

component: Tornado
failureMode: Initiating event frequency
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Probability of a design basis tornado of 175 mph striking the Idaho Chemical Processing Plant, quoted from DOE/EA-0306 (reference 10.17) and used as the tornado initiator frequency.

component: High wind
failureMode: Initiating event frequency, wind above the design basis wind
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Probability of exceeding the design basis wind of 95 mph, set for a 10,000 year return period (UCRL-15910). Note [2]: bounded by the TSEC, TBOP and LONP initiators.

component: Volcanism
failureMode: Initiating event frequency, any eruption
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Section 10.5 gives lava flow recurrence frequencies in the range of 1E-5 per year, with an eruption reaching the site once every 80,000 to 100,000 years (DOE/EIS-0136).

component: Volcanism
failureMode: Initiating event frequency, eruption affecting EBR-II, upper bound
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Printed as less than 1.0E-8 per year.

component: External flooding
failureMode: Initiating event frequency, upper bound
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Printed as less than 1.0E-8 per year. The site is at 5120 ft and the Big Lost River is 11 miles away at 4850 ft.

component: Aircraft impact
failureMode: Initiating event frequency, crash into EBR-II
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Table value. The calculation in Section 10.8 prints 8.4E-9 crashes per year.

component: Turbine generator missile
failureMode: Initiating event frequency, highest value in the range
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Printed as a range of 3.1E-4 to 3.5E-5 per turbine year, from turbine failures in nuclear and non-nuclear service corrected for nuclear units (reference 10.20).

component: Turbine generator missile
failureMode: Initiating event frequency, lowest value in the range
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Printed as a range of 3.1E-4 to 3.5E-5 per turbine year, from turbine failures in nuclear and non-nuclear service corrected for nuclear units (reference 10.20).

component: Internal flooding
failureMode: Initiating event frequency, upper bound
table: Table 10.2. Summary of External Event Initiating Events and Sequences
method: Printed as less than 1E-10 per year. Note [6]: damage from unprotected loss of the primary pump clutches, with the other sequences bounded by loss of heat sink.

component: Primary tank
failureMode: Primary tank leak event
table: Section 10.2.2.2 Primary Coolant Inventory (LOSA) Functional Failure, text on page 10-9
method: Printed as the probability of the primary tank leak event, with no time unit.

component: Primary tank and guard vessel
failureMode: Breach of both the primary tank and the guard vessel, upper bound
table: Section 10.2.2.2 Primary Coolant Inventory (LOSA) Functional Failure, text on page 10-9
method: Printed as below the 1E-10 cutoff.

component: Sodium and NaK piping
failureMode: Piping failure rate per foot of piping
table: Section 10.2.3.2 Initiating Event Frequency, text on page 10-15
method: Rate per hour and per foot of piping, used with reactor runs of 2400 hours and about three runs per year to give the leak initiating frequencies of Table 10.2.

component: Sodium and NaK piping breach
failureMode: Leak to rupture ratio for 1 inch pipes, value quoted from reference 10.8
table: Section 10.2.3.5 Limited Leak vs Rupture, text on page 10-20
method: Ratio of leak frequency to rupture frequency. Probabilistic fracture mechanics and LWR experience (Beliczey and Schulz 1987).

component: Sodium and NaK piping breach
failureMode: Leak to rupture ratio for pipes larger than 10 inches, value quoted from reference 10.8
table: Section 10.2.3.5 Limited Leak vs Rupture, text on page 10-20
method: Ratio of leak frequency to rupture frequency. Probabilistic fracture mechanics and LWR experience (Beliczey and Schulz 1987).

component: Sodium and NaK piping breach
failureMode: Leak to guillotine break ratio, value quoted from NUREG/CR-4407
table: Section 10.2.3.5 Limited Leak vs Rupture, text on page 10-20
method: Ratio of leak frequency to rupture frequency. Pipe break frequency estimates for nuclear power plants (reference 10.9).

component: Sodium and NaK piping breach
failureMode: Leak to rupture ratio for all pipe sizes, value quoted from reference 10.10
table: Section 10.2.3.5 Limited Leak vs Rupture, text on page 10-20
method: Ratio of leak frequency to rupture frequency. Older pipe and vessel failure study (Thomas 1981).

component: Sodium and NaK piping breach
failureMode: Leak to rupture ratio selected for this analysis
table: Section 10.2.3.5 Limited Leak vs Rupture, text on page 10-20
method: Ratio of leak frequency to rupture frequency. Gives the conditional rupture probability of 1.0E-2 used in the event trees.

component: Fire suppression for a shutdown cooler NaK rupture with remote ARGON system actuation
failureMode: Suppression failure, sensitivity value
table: Section 10.2.5 Planned Modifications to Address Vulnerability, text on page 10-27
method: Remote actuation failure judged no worse than event RHU001CL, failure to manually scram without a scram signal. Replaces the suppression failure of 5E-1 in a sensitivity case.

component: Loss of constant power
failureMode: Frequency used to bound non-sodium fires
table: Section 10.3.1 Plant Impacts From Fire Initiators, text on page 10-28
method: The worst non-sodium fire disables the constant power supply to the primary pump clutches, and the loss of constant power frequency bounds this case.

component: Tornado
failureMode: Annual probability of a tornado striking the INEL
table: Section 10.4.1 Tornadoes, text on page 10-31
method: Quoted from DOE/EIS-0136 (reference 10.14).

component: Tornado within the INEL boundaries
failureMode: Tornadoes reported in more than 23 years of observation
table: Section 10.4.1 Tornadoes, text on page 10-30
method: No tornado reported within the INEL in more than 23 years. Two low-intensity tornadoes and 10 vortex clouds were sighted within 10 miles, with no period printed.

component: Tornado
failureMode: Design basis tornado of 175 mph striking the Idaho Chemical Processing Plant
table: Section 10.4.1 Tornadoes, text on page 10-31
method: Quoted from DOE/EA-0306 (reference 10.17). Used as the tornado initiator frequency.

component: Loss of primary heat sink (TSEC and TBOP initiators)
failureMode: Approximate initiating frequency quoted for comparison with high winds
table: Section 10.4.2 High Winds, text on page 10-34
method: Printed as about 1 per year.

component: Lava flow at the ANL-W site
failureMode: Lava flows in the past 500,000 years
table: Section 10.5 Volcanism, text on page 10-36
method: Count from cores of wells at the site, exposure in years. No rate is printed for this count.

component: Aircraft on an airway
failureMode: Inflight crash rate per aircraft mile
table: Section 10.8 Aircraft Impact, text on pages 10-39 and 10-40
method: Standard Review Plan 3.5.1.6 (NUREG-0800) value, crashes per aircraft mile, used in P = C N A / W.

component: Aircraft impact
failureMode: Crash frequency into EBR-II
table: Section 10.8 Aircraft Impact, text on pages 10-39 and 10-40
method: P = C N A / W with C = 4.0E-10 per aircraft mile, N = 4220 flights per year (2920 IFR flights, about 100 vortex test flights and about 100 VFR operations per month), A = 0.01 square miles and W = 2 miles. Table 10.2 prints 8.2E-9.

component: Turbine missile damage to critical reactor components, commercial LWRs
failureMode: Probability of serious consequences, highest value in the range quoted from reference 10.19
table: Section 10.10 Turbine Missiles, text on page 10-41
method: Printed as a range of 1E-10 to 1E-12 per year from studies of Westinghouse and General Electric LWRs (Bush 1973).

component: Turbine missile damage to critical reactor components, commercial LWRs
failureMode: Probability of serious consequences, lowest value in the range quoted from reference 10.19
table: Section 10.10 Turbine Missiles, text on page 10-41
method: Printed as a range of 1E-10 to 1E-12 per year from studies of Westinghouse and General Electric LWRs (Bush 1973).

component: Turbine missile
failureMode: Probability of striking a critical target
table: Section 10.10 Turbine Missiles, text on page 10-41
method: From the turbine failure reassessment (reference 10.20).

component: Turbine missile striking the EBR-II main control room
failureMode: Worst case frequency, personnel risk
table: Section 10.10 Turbine Missiles, text on page 10-41
method: Upper initiator frequency of 3.1E-4 per turbine year times the strike probability of 1.0E-3. Table 10.2 note [5] states that it is a personnel risk and not core or plant damage.

component: Wet pipe fire protection sprinkler head
failureMode: Inadvertent actuation, environmental failures (high temperature due to steam)
table: Section 10.11 Internal Floods, text on page 10-43
method: Counts from reference 10.23 for a population of 60,000 heads over 30 years. Exposure 60,000 x 30 = 1.8E6 head-years, multiplied out here.

component: Wet pipe fire protection sprinkler head
failureMode: Inadvertent actuation, failures due to maintenance
table: Section 10.11 Internal Floods, text on page 10-43
method: Counts from reference 10.23 for a population of 60,000 heads over 30 years. Exposure 60,000 x 30 = 1.8E6 head-years, multiplied out here.

component: Wet pipe fire protection sprinkler head
failureMode: Inadvertent actuation rate, all causes
table: Section 10.11 Internal Floods, text on page 10-43
method: Calculated in the report from 3 environmental and 5 maintenance failures in a population of 60,000 for 30 years (reference 10.23).

component: Primary pump clutch control cabinet
failureMode: Water from an inadvertent sprinkler actuation causing loss of both primary pumps, initiating frequency
table: Section 10.11 Internal Floods, text on page 10-43
method: Assumed equal to the failure rate of the single sprinkler in the area, since the cabinet has no spray shield.

component: Loss of normal power (LONP)
failureMode: Frequency from causes other than sprinkler actuation, quoted for comparison
table: Section 10.11 Internal Floods, text on page 10-43
method: Printed as 10^-1. A sprinkler induced loss of normal power is subsumed into this frequency.

component: Double pump loss of flow, group B (LF2B)
failureMode: Internal initiating event frequency quoted for comparison
table: Section 10.11 Internal Floods, text on page 10-43
method: Quoted from the internal events analysis to compare with the clutch cabinet water initiator.

component: Event tree heading LMFD, liquid metal fire detection, secondary sodium fire in containment (SSFR)
failureMode: Failure to detect the fire
table: Figure 10.3. Event Tree Results for Secondary Sodium Fire in Containment
method: Screening value for failure to detect a liquid metal fire before core and structural damage (Section 10.2.3.3). Eight photoelectric smoke detectors in six zones are smoke tested every six months and have not failed since installation in 1980.

component: Event tree heading RFIR, reactor shutdown, secondary sodium fire in containment (SSFR)
failureMode: Failure of manual and automatic scram

component: Fuel handling computer and positioning hardware

failureMode: Second 1.5 dollar loading error given a first error
table: Appendix A, Section 5.2.1 The Initiating Event Tree, text on page A-25
method: Printed as 1 x 0.161 x 0.091, since a companion error is assumed highly probable once one error is made. Two such errors are needed to overcome the 3.0 dollar margin, giving 2.0E-5 per subrun (event CCG005RG).

component: Safety rods (fuel handling trip)
failureMode: Fail to scram on demand
table: Appendix A, Section 5.2.4 Safety Rod Trip, text on page A-27
method: Estimate 1/2 x (1/475) for zero failures in 475 demands. With about one use per subrun this is also 1.1E-3 per subrun. Page A-28 calls it an experience rated value of about 1E-3 per demand.

component: Safety rods (fuel handling trip)
failureMode: Fail to trip, judgment of another PRA team member, upper bound
table: Appendix A, Section 5.4 Discussion of the Event Probability, text on page A-28

component: Numerically controlled positioning system (NCPS)
failureMode: Mechanical positioning error in core fuel movements
table: Appendix A, Section 5.4 Discussion of the Event Probability, text on page A-28

component: Fueled subassembly dropped into the core
